hints.junior: The test hardcoded fullName: "Jane Doe" forever. The backend renamed the field, production broke, the test stayed green.
hints.mid: A hand-written fixture is a snapshot of a belief about the API frozen on the day someone wrote it, nothing keeps it current.
hints.staff: This is a contract problem, not a diligence problem, more careful fixtures just add more independent copies of a possibly-wrong belief.

hints.junior: Same field rename, two test files, one guesses at the shape, one is generated from a shared schema.
hints.mid: The hand-typed fixture has zero relationship to the real endpoint, the schema-derived mock is downstream of the same contract the backend honors.
hints.staff: Notice where each fails, the hand-typed version fails in production weeks later, the schema-derived version fails loudly in CI at the PR that broke it.

hints.junior: MSW intercepts the real network request your component already makes, it doesn't replace your fetch code with a fake function.
hints.mid: Pairing MSW with a schema shared with the backend means a mismatch is a build-time failure instead of a silent runtime one.
hints.staff: MSW plus an unvalidated hand-maintained schema is the same drift problem one level removed, the schema has to trace back to something the backend enforces.

hints.junior: MSW is the interception mechanism, not the source of truth, the real fix is the shared schema it's paired with.
hints.mid: Generate frontend types and mock schemas from the backend's own OpenAPI spec rather than hand-writing a frontend-side approximation.
hints.staff: Run the same contract tests on backend PRs that touch the shared schema too, a backend-only change is exactly the failure mode this exists to catch.

sections.junior: Hey! Today's case is about a hardcoded test fixture that stayed green for months after the real API it was mocking had already changed shape.
The fix is Mock Service Worker, intercepting the real network call your component makes, paired with a schema shared with the real backend.
Compare a hand typed fixture against an MSW handler using a schema derived mock, both facing the same backend field rename.
Stop hand typing mock API responses in tests. Use MSW with a schema shared with the real backend, so a shape mismatch fails loudly instead of silently.
